blocks.text: “We define the One China policy. We define it. Not them.” Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. was responding to Beijing’s protest over Taiwan’s plan to open a representative office in Cebu. He later added that how the Philippines implements its One China policy is “none of their business.” The Department of Foreign Affairs used more diplomatic language, saying that the policy remains unchanged while allowing economic, cultural, and functional cooperation with Taiwan. Secretary Teodoro was right. Beijing has become increasingly insistent that other countries follow its One China principle, including China’s own understanding of what contacts with Taiwan should be allowed. […]...
